body.statement: For every \(S\in\mathcal I\) and every mechanism in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(G)\), \(\det(C_{S,S})\ne0\) and \(K_S^{B,\varepsilon}(x)=\mathcal L(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x)\). Moreover, \(R_S(C)\varepsilon=X_{X\setminus S}-T_S(C)X_S\) observationally. Hence the observational law together with \(\{T_S(C):S\in\mathcal I\}\) determines the entire joint tuple of affine response kernels, including every cancellation and every observationally invisible source.
body.justification: This identity reduces multi-regime full-law comparison to one observational mixture law and finitely many common response matrices.
body.gap: Bongers et al. establish intervention solvability, while the required principal-resolvent pushforward and its source-visibility consequence are not their equivalence result.
body.consumer: The coupled compiler uses the identity to avoid fitting or aligning a different latent-source representation in each intervention regime.
